entries.text: Bus body. The body is painted school-bus yellow so drivers can see it from far away.
Roof. The roof is rounded and strong. It keeps the rain out and the children safe inside.
Hood and engine. The engine sits out in front under the hood, so the driver can hear it and fix it.
Driver cab. The driver sits high up with a big steering wheel and mirrors on every side.
Doors. The doors open so children can board one at a time.
Seats and belts. Blue bench seats line both sides, and every seat has its own belt.
Walkway. A straight walkway runs down the middle, all the way to the back door.
Stop arm. The red stop sign folds out and tells every car: stop, children are crossing.
Warning lights. Red and amber lights flash on the roof when the bus is picking children up.
Wheels. Four big black tires grip the road. The front pair turns to steer the bus.
Yellow shell. Yellow panels join together to make the bus body.
Side windows. Five passenger windows on each side bring light into the bus.
Rub rail. The black bars along the side are rub rails. They take the bumps instead of the paint.
Skirt panel. A low panel closes the gap between the floor and the road.
Rounded roof. The curved roof covers the cabin and sheds rain.
Roof hatch. A release handle lets an adult open the emergency roof hatch.
Roof bows. Curved roof bows support the skin above the cabin.
Hood. The hood covers the engine at the front of the bus.
Grille. Air rushes through the grille to cool the hot engine.
Headlights. Two round headlights light the road on dark winter mornings.
Front bumper. A thick black bumper is the first thing to meet a bump.
Engine assembly. The engine block, valve cover and pipes sit on strong mounts.
Radiator and fan. Coolant carries heat to the radiator, and airflow carries it away.
Steering wheel. The steering wheel lets the driver guide the bus.
Dashboard. Dials show how fast the bus goes and how much fuel is left.
Driver seat. A raised driver seat faces the windshield and controls.
Windshield. The windshield lets the driver see ahead through clear glass.
Crossing mirror. Extra mirrors in front show the driver the blind spot right at the bumper.
Door leaves. Two door leaves swing inward on hinges at the outer edges.
Door glass. Clear panes let the driver see the entry steps and people outside.
Entry steps. Three non-slip treads lead from the entrance to the cabin floor.
Emergency door. A rear emergency door lines up with the clear center aisle.
Seat cushions. Blue padded cushions sit above sturdy seat frames.
High seat backs. Tall padded backs separate the rows of seats.
Seat belts. A shoulder strap and lap strap meet at a buckle.
Seat legs. Steel legs bolt every bench straight down to the floor.
Walkway floor. A ribbed rubber floor gives shoes something to grip.
Entry handrails. Entry handrails help children steady themselves on the steps.
Rear walkway. The walkway reaches all the way to the emergency door.
Stop sign. The red octagonal sign unfolds to warn nearby drivers.
Folding arm. A hinged arm holds the sign beside the bus.
Arm lamp. Small red lamps help the stop sign stand out.
Red warning lights. Red warning lights signal that the bus has stopped for children.
Amber warning lights. Amber warning lights signal that the bus is preparing to stop.
Light housing. A black housing surrounds each pair of warning lamps.
Tires. Four black tires hold the whole bus up off the road.
Tread. Raised tread blocks leave channels around the tire.
Wheel hub. A shiny steel hub in the middle holds the wheel onto the axle.
Wheel arch. A curved arch over each wheel keeps the splash outside.
